synoptic.summary: The Pacific ridge has slid south and a weakening trough with a cold front crosses northern Utah early Saturday. The Salt Lake airport forecast has the front around 05:00 Saturday, with showers until about 08:00. Behind it, flow from 300°–330° runs 27–32 kt about 1,800 ft above the landings and 30–42 kt about 3,500 ft above through Saturday morning. Saturday afternoon stays gusty from 320° (airport forecast 15 G25 kt), and the flow aloft eases to 12–24 kt by evening. High pressure returns Sunday with light flow from 160°–200° in the lowest levels. On Monday a weak trough grazes northern Utah, with flow from 150°–170° at the launches and a small shower chance. Thunder chances are 0–3% all period, but showers on Saturday morning and again Monday morning can hide virga.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: A cold front will begin to cross over the terminal around 12Z Saturday accompanied by rain showers and CIGS below 5kft resulting in a 30% chance of MVFR conditions through 15Z. The first chance of rain showers will begin around 7z Saturday, but the greatest chance of precipitation wont occur until the front passes over the terminal around 12-15z.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport (KSLC) sea-level pressure was 1018.7 mb at 19:54 Fri, down from 1027.3 mb 23 h earlier and 1.1 mb in the last hour, as the trough and front arrive. Expect rising pressure and gusty flow from 300°–340° behind the front on Saturday, then the brief high on Sunday.

observations.summary: Friday evening only (18:35–19:45 local), about 12 h before the first slot and before the cold front. These readings say little about Saturday morning. Ahead of the front, the Utah Valley stations show flow from 155°–185°: Spanish Fork at 13 kt, Alpine at 9 kt, Lehi at 7 kt. That matches the airport forecasts (140°–160° at 5–8 kt overnight). Salt Lake and Provo airports are near calm. Point of the Mountain and Draper returned no observations. South Valley Regional's last wind is from 18:15 (180° at 4 kt) and its 18:35 report has no wind.
